faq.q: Why use titanium for titanium derailleur limit screw?
faq.a: Grade 5 (Ti-6Al-4V) provides ideal wear resistance, fatigue strength, and 40% weight saving vs steel for drivetrain components. Grade 9 for fasteners requiring cold heading.

faq.q: How is a titanium derailleur limit screw manufactured?
faq.a: A typical titanium derailleur limit screw is manufactured using CNC machining of tooth profile; Thread rolling; Swiss-type turning. Each step is critical to achieving the required mechanical properties and dimensional tolerances.

faq.q: What are the alternatives to Grade 5 Ti-6Al-4V for titanium derailleur limit screw?
faq.a: Stainless steel (heavier, less fatigue life), aluminum (lower strength)

faq.q: What standards apply to titanium derailleur limit screw?
faq.a: Titanium Derailleur Limit Screw components are typically manufactured to ASTM B348. Additional customer-specific specifications may apply depending on the application and regulatory requirements.
